This is a preliminary sort of finding that does suggest, at least for the laboratory test, that rather brief breaks help the brain "reconfigure" or solidify what has been learned. The specific applicability for this is rather important for stroke patients, see here:

"Our results suggest that it may be important to optimize the timing and configuration of rest intervals when implementing rehabilitative treatments in stroke patients or when learning to play the piano in normal volunteers," said Dr. Cohen. "Whether these results apply to other forms of learning and memory formation remains an open question."

Limitations are that, obviously, these are motor and repetition tasks not complex cognitive ones. Nevertheless, other research has shown benefits of spaced repetition with complex cognitive tasks like language acquisition and mathematics. In general, it appears the best thing to do when learning any skill is to take a few seconds or minutes in between to let your brain settle.
